## Apple — Operating Margin, Last 8 Quarters

| Quarter ended | Fiscal qtr | Operating income | Revenue | **Operating margin** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-09-28 | FQ4'24 | $29,591M *(derived)* | $94,930M *(derived)* | **31.17%** |
| 2024-12-28 | FQ1'25 | $42,832M | $124,300M | **34.46%** |
| 2025-03-29 | FQ2'25 | $29,589M | $95,359M | **31.03%** |
| 2025-06-28 | FQ3'25 | $28,202M | $94,036M | **29.99%** |
| 2025-09-27 | FQ4'25 | $32,427M *(derived)* | $102,466M *(derived)* | **31.65%** |
| 2025-12-27 | FQ1'26 | $50,852M | $143,756M | **35.37%** |
| 2026-03-28 | FQ2'26 | $35,885M | $111,184M | **32.28%** |
| 2026-06-27 | FQ3'26 | $35,695M | $109,417M | **32.62%** |

*Provenance note:* the two September quarters (FQ4'24 and FQ4'25) are **derived** figures — synthesized as FY minus Q1–Q3 from the 10-K filed 2025-10-31, not directly filed quarterly facts. All other quarters come from directly filed `OperatingIncomeLoss` / `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` tags in the 10-Qs filed 2026-01-30, 2026-05-01 and 2026-07-31.

### What the trend shows

**1. Strong seasonality dominates the quarter-to-quarter pattern.** The December quarter is consistently the margin peak (34.46% in FQ1'25, 35.37% in FQ1'26), reflecting holiday operating leverage on a much larger revenue base. The June quarter is the seasonal trough (29.99% in FQ3'25).

**2. Underneath the seasonality, margins have stepped up.** Comparing like fiscal quarters year over year, every pair improved: FQ1 34.46% → 35.37%, FQ2 31.03% → 32.28%, FQ3 29.99% → 32.62%, and FQ4 31.17% → 31.65%. The FQ3 comparison is the largest improvement in the set.

**3. The improvement is being driven at the gross-margin line.** Gross margin rose steadily across the window — 46.22% (FQ4'24) → 46.88% → 47.05% → 46.49% → 47.18% → 48.16% → 49.27% → **50.06%** in the most recent quarter, the first reading above 50% in the series. That ~4-point gross margin expansion from the start of the window is larger than the operating margin expansion over the same span (31.17% → 32.62%), which implies operating expenses grew somewhat faster than revenue and absorbed part of the gross-margin gain.

**4. Most recent quarter (FQ3'26, ended 2026-06-27):** operating margin of 32.62% on $109,417M revenue, up slightly from 32.28% the prior quarter despite revenue declining sequentially from $111,184M — margin held up on the record 50.06% gross margin. Net margin was 27.23%.

One caveat on the FQ4'24 datapoint: its net margin of 15.52% is far below every other quarter in the series while its operating margin (31.17%) is in line — the gap sits below the operating line, so the operating-margin trend itself isn't distorted by it.
